followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

**Capability fit:** This is a small, well-defined algebra problem with a single correct answer — a reasoning/retrieval-style task, not creative generation. Lapwing has the edge on the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 80.3 vs 75.9, GPQA Diamond 62.5 vs 56.2, IFEval 90.4 vs 85.3), which makes it the safer pick for clean, correct step-by-step math. The internal eval categories that would matter here (Extraction & Retrieval) also favor Lapwing by a margin above the variance threshold.

**Preference fit:** The query is explicitly polite, warm, and collaborative ("Could you help me work through this?", "thank you so much"). Lapwing self-reports rising preference win rates exactly along that dimension — good-faith, cooperative requests are its top-rated tasks. This task also has low latitude and zero novelty requirement, so it avoids Lapwing's one documented aversion (open-ended creative invention).

So both axes pointed the same way: Lapwing is at least as capable on this task type and actively prefers this kind of interaction, with no countervailing weakness triggered. Avocet had no offsetting advantage — its preferences here were near-neutral and its benchmarks slightly lower.
